answerBox.snippet: At high temperatures (37.8 C-43.3 C), infectious virus could not be detected after 2-7 days, whereas at lower temperatures (10 C-21.1 C), it took up to 112 days for virus to decrease to undetectable levels.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: How contagious is Newcastle disease?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: The disease is very contagious. When the virus is introduced into a susceptible flock, virtually all the birds will be infected within two to six days.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: How is the Newcastle disease virus transmitted?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: NDV is primarily transmitted via inhalation or ingestion of virus shed in feces and respiratory secretions by infected birds for variable lengths of time [3, 4, 20]. Some virus isolates have been found to be transmitted through the egg to the hatching chick [21].

peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Newcastle disease is successfully controlled by vaccination in commercial poultry, but no treatment is available.
